Visual analysis confirms that the integration of PConv and CSAM enables the model to accurately focus on lesion regions, aligning with the diagnostic logic of agricultural experts. Rather than serving only as a standalone classifier, PCSAM‐YOLO functions as a high‐performance inference core capable of supporting downstream decision‐making and automated management recommendations in complex agricultural IoT environments.

title: Mapping of Crop Planting Structures Under Limited Training Samples Using TabPFN and Sentinel-2 Time Series Data
abstract: Accurate mapping of crop planting structures is critical for precision agriculture, yet it remains challenging in rugged terrain with fragmented fields, frequent cloud contamination, and limited high-quality training samples. This study evaluates an integrated framework combining recursive feature elimination (RFE) and the pretrained Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) for small-sample crop classification using Sentinel-2 time-series data in Yuxi City, located on the western margin of the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. A multidimensional feature set integrating spectral and temporal vegetation indices and textural and geospatial information was constructed and optimized via RFE. The TabPFN model achieved an overall accuracy (OA) of 96.27%, a kappa coefficient of 0.9558, and a macro-F1 score of 0.956 in the main validation. In repeated small-sample experiments, TabPFN maintained a mean OA of 90.60% at a 30% training-sample ratio and 82.89% at a 10% ratio. RF-guided feature ranking and ablation analyses suggested that temporal vegetation indices were important predictors, followed by early-season spectral characteristics, textural features, and supplementary geospatial information. Overall, these findings indicate that RFE-TabPFN is a feasible option for 10 m crop mapping in Yuxi under limited training samples, while its broader applicability still requires further testing across additional years, regions, and cropping systems.

title: Intelligent Crop Protection: AI Powered Detection and Diagnosis of Plant Diseases
abstract: Agriculture is the main factor that supports India’s economy, but, the continuation of crop diseases cause significant losses of yields every year which threatens food security and farmers incomes. This research presents a smart, CNN-based system for the automatic identification and explanation of plant leaf diseases.The model was trained on a large and diverse dataset of more than 27000 images of 4 crops and 22 disease classes. By using state-of-the-art preprocessing and feature extraction, the CNN attained a validation accuracy of 92.57%, which is in line with high precision and strong generalization power. The trained model is housed in a Flask-based web application that offers instant disease identification along with easy-to-understand treatment suggestions, farm care instructions, soil management tips, and some care tips. By cutting the overuse of pesticides and promoting data-driven farming, the system is helping to sustain agriculture and increase crop yields. The next development will be an offline mobile version to provide more access and convenience in remote farming areas.

title: Early Paddy Disease Detection & Sustainable Farming for South Indian Farmers
abstract: In Southern India, paddy farmers frequently experience significant crop losses and financial strain due to delayed detection of plant diseases. To address this challenge, we propose a predictive monitoring system that enables early detection of paddy diseases and helps prevent large-scale yield damage. The proposed framework is designed to combine a YOLOv8based image analysis module with an LSTM-based environmental forecasting component that considers factors such as rainfall, humidity, and temperature for early disease risk prediction. The current implementation and experimental evaluation primarily focus on the YOLOv8-based disease detection module, while the remaining components are considered part of the proposed future framework. Additionally, the system design includes geospatial analysis through Google Earth Engine for regional disease risk visualization and a low-cost, multilingual user interface to support ease of use by farmers. The initial deployment targets two districts in Southern India, contributing to more sustainable and resilient farming practices.

title: An interpretable trait-based machine learning framework for mandarin varietal discrimination using morphogeometric signatures
Smart Farming Through Deep Learning: Automated Plant Disease Detection Using CNN Models
abstract: Plant disease is still a big challenges in agricultural production across the world. Manual examination alone can be time-consuming, labour-intensive, and error-prone, and is hard to be extended to large- scale cultivation. To overcome these constraints, we propose a CNN-based method for automated early detection of plant diseases. The model is trained on a large-scale dataset of more than 87000 images of 38 classes of healthy and infected plant leaves. Prior to training, a structured preprocessing pipeline including resize, normalize, and data augmentation on images to increase variability within samples and reduce the risk of overfitting is applied to all images. The CNN model consists of convolution and pooling layers with a final fully connected layer and the optimization is performed with Adam optimizer. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method yields an accuracy of 96%. As consequence of the comprehensive augmentation strategy, the model is also extended to unsee samples and obtains better performance than other famous architectures like AlexNet and VGG16. These results underscore the ability of deep learning to facilitate precision agriculture through early disease detection, which allows farmers to make better management decisions and improve yield and farm sustainability.

title: PlantDiff: A diffusion model for high-fidelity plant image generation with Discrete Wavelet Transform and Context-Augmented Cross Attention
YOLOv8-Ghost-QWA: A Lightweight Model with Quadro-Weighted Attention for Tomato Maturity Segmentation
abstract: Robust, real-time recognition of tomato maturity in unconstrained field conditions remains a critical bottleneck for autonomous harvesting platforms, as manual methods are costly and labor-intensive. Existing approaches, such as Vision Transformer-based models and YOLO variants with attention modules, often overfit to controlled environments, struggle with surface anomalies, and demand excessive computational resources unsuitable for edge devices in robotic harvesters. To address these challenges, we introduce the modified YOLOv8-nano architecture, which incorporates Ghost convolutions to reduce feature redundancy and a lightweight adaptive fusion module (Quadro-Weighted Attention, QWA) block that adaptively fuses Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) with 3 × 3 Triplet Attention (TA) via a learnable sigmoid gate. In addition, we present the iTomato-Seg-UA dataset, which spans three ripening stages (green, ripening, and ripe) under diverse illumination, backgrounds, cultivars, and anomalies (cracks, catfacing, and zippering). The proposed YOLOv8-Ghost-QWA model demonstrates a 77% F1 score and 82% mAP on the merged test subset while requiring 39% fewer parameters and 25% fewer GFLOPs compared to vanilla YOLOv8. These results demonstrate a competitive efficiency-accuracy trade-off for maturity segmentation on edge devices, highlighting the practical potential of lightweight attention-based enhancements.

title: Multi-Objective Optimization for a Robust Deep Learning Model in Plant Image Classification: A Review with Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) techniques for the enhancement of Deep Learning (DL)-based plant image classification by jointly addressing competing objectives such as classification accuracy, inference speed, generalization capability, and computational efficiency. Unlike existing research that treats DL architectures or optimization strategies in isolation, this work systematically integrates MOO principles with state-of-the-art DL models across the entire learning pipeline, including feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and neural architecture search. Key evolutionary and hybrid MOO algorithms - such as NSGA-II, MOEA/D, MOPSO, and SPEA2 – were critically analyzed with respect to their applicability in agricultural imaging tasks. Practical challenges were further highlighted, arising from environmental variability, dataset imbalance, and field deployment constraints. By synthesizing current trends, identifying research gaps, and outlining future directions, this study positions MOO as a promising paradigm for developing robust, resource-aware, and field-deployable AI systems for precision agriculture.

title: Assessing the generalization of geospatial embeddings for temporaltransfer in land cover classification
Fractional transform assisted image recognition with genetic diagnostic calibration for plant disease detection
abstract: Early and accurate detection of plant diseases is essential to ensure agricultural productivity, minimize crop losses, and maintain food security. Conventional image-based recognition systems, though promising, often face limitations when deployed in real-world farming environments. Variations in lighting, overlapping disease symptoms, and differences between laboratory-curated datasets and field images reduce their robustness and reliability. At the same time, genetic diagnostic tools such as CRISPR-based assays have demonstrated great potential for molecular-level confirmation, yet these remain separated from image recognition workflows, thereby limiting their practicality in field applications. This research introduces FRaGILE, a novel Fractional-transform-augmented Genetic-diagnostics-Integrated Learning framework. The framework uniquely integrates fractional spectral–spatial transforms with deep learning architectures to enhance disease classification accuracy. Fractional Fourier and wavelet transforms are applied to capture lesion texture and frequency features at varying fractional orders, while convolutional and transformer backbones are trained to learn discriminative and invariant representations. Additionally, a Bayesian calibration layer incorporates optional CRISPR-based diagnostic signals, improving confidence estimation and reducing false positives in ambiguous cases. Experimental validation is conducted using multi-source plant pathology datasets, including hyperspectral and visible light benchmarks. Results indicate consistent improvements in F1-score and AUROC compared to baseline convolutional networks. Sensitivity analyses reveal that fractional transform orders within the range of 0.6 to 0.9 yield optimal performance, while the incorporation of fractional Laplacian enhancements further strengthens detection under variable illumination. The proposed system is implemented on a hardware–software stack suitable for smartphones and edge devices, enabling field-level deployment. The hybrid workflow, which begins with image-based triage and leverages genetic confirmation when necessary, establishes a practical, scalable, and scientifically rigorous approach to plant disease detection. By fusing phenotypic and genotypic insights, FRaGILE sets the foundation for more reliable, actionable, and sustainable disease management in agriculture. This study focuses on the challenge of accurate plant disease detection by integrating fractional-transform-based image recognition with genetically informed diagnostic calibration. Conventional image-only approaches often work poorly with early-stage infections and visually ambiguous symptoms due to various factors such as lighting variability, background clutter, and inter-class similarity. In an attempt to bridge this gap, we introduce FRaGILE: Fractional Representation and Genetic Integrated Learning Engine, a hybrid framework that synergistically fuses the phenotypic image features with simulated CRISPR-based molecular evidence. The central research questions which this study tried to answer are: RQ1: Does the fractional-order transform improve robustness of features against noise and variation in illumination? (RQ2) Does calibration of genetic diagnostic improve the confidence and reliability in classification? The proposed hybrid framework can perform better than the state-of-the-art deep learning models on different plant disease datasets.

title: Plant Leaf Disease Classification Using a Multi-Scale Attention Network
abstract: Monitoring plant health and increasing crop productivity depend on the prompt identification of plant diseases. The diagnostic process is challenging due to the fact that infection symptoms might vary in size. This study addresses this issue by introducing a small-sized and multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN) model designed for the identification of plant diseases in leaf images. In order to capture disease symptoms at various resolutions, this model uses multi-scale attention blocks, each of which has two convolutional branches with different kernel sizes. To enforce concentration on key features, a channel attention block is added to improve the representational power of the model. To achieve a balance between model performance and complexity, a few layers are used to create a small-sized architecture. The model has nearly one million parameters. Two plant disease datasets were used for evaluating the performance of the developed model. Compared to recent models, our model recorded SOTA performance with lower computational complexity. The accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were 99.68%, 99.51%, 99.62%, and 99.56%, respectively, on the PlantVillage dataset, and 96.64%, 96.63%, 96.64%, and 96.63% on the SAR-CLD-2024 cotton disease dataset. Further analyses highlighted the importance of a multi-scale framework and the incorporation of the attention block.

title: Approaches to detecting peanut diseases based on remote sensing and artificial intelligence : machine learning and deep learning
abstract: Peanuts (Arachis hypogaea L.) are a major oil seed crop grown in tropical and subtropical regions. However, each harvest is compromised by leaf diseases that affect not only yield but also quality. Traditional diagnostic methods based on visual observation have several limitations: cost, time, and technical expertise. To address these limitations, approaches based on remote sensing (multispectral and hyperspectral imaging) and artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), have been developed. Unlike previous reviews, this study presents a comparative and critical analysis of ML and DL techniques, as well as a conceptual framework integrating remote sensing and AI for the detection of peanut diseases. This analysis highlights the main limitations of current methodologies and identifies key challenges while providing directions for future research.

title: Comparative Study of Deep Transfer Learning Models for Classifying Different Types of Diseases in Paddy
abstract: The early identification of rice leaf diseases protects food supplies and enhances farm productivity. The traditional approach to manual inspection takes too much time while delivering results that depend on personal judgment and cannot handle inspection needs for extensive farming territories. This study introduces HybridRiceNet which functions as a deep transfer learning system featuring hybrid attention mechanisms to achieve precise identification of paddy leaf diseases. The system uses pre-trained convolutional neural networks together with an attention system to enhance its ability to identify essential features needed for disease detection. The researchers applied advanced preprocessing methods together with data augmentation techniques to achieve better results on small dataset testing. The researchers assessed the model using a public database of rice leaf diseases which contains four categories: Brown Spot, Leaf Blast, Hispa, and Healthy. The experimental results show that HybridRiceNet achieves better results than standard transfer learning models through its 97.1% accuracy rate which exceeds the performance of VGG16, ResNet50, InceptionV3, and MobileNetV2 models. The system uses explainable AI methods to make its operations easier for users to understand. The results demonstrate that HybridRiceNet functions as a dependable and effective system for use in smart agricultural systems which require immediate processing capabilities.

title: An Explainable Hybrid CNN–ViT Model for Detecting Leaf Diseases: A Dual-Interpretability Approach Using Heatmaps and SHAP on Coconut, Banana, and Sugarcane
abstract: This paper proposes an explainable hybrid deep learning ensemble for multi-crop leaf disease classification across the three crops: coconut, banana, and sugarcane. Three architectures: ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, and ViT-Small are trained independently and combined using rank-based exponential weighted averaging voting, achieving 99.79% overall accuracy, macro precision of 99.88%, recall of 99.90%, and F1-score of 99.89%. across 18 disease classes, including an outstanding perfect 100% accuracy on sugarcane. A three-layer explainability framework integrates Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) heatmaps, Attention Rollout for Vision Transformer attention visualization, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) for unified feature attribution. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid ensemble outperforms all individual models and other related works models while producing interpretable, biologically meaningful visual explanations suitable for adoption by agricultural technicians.

title: An artificial intelligence and hybrid edge computing framework for precision agriculture disease management system
Improved YOLOv8 for Tree Species Detection Using Bark Texture Features
abstract: Tree bark is a relatively stable visual feature for tree species detection because it remains visible throughout the year and is less affected by seasonal changes than leaves or flowers. However, bark-texture-based tree species detection in natural scenes remains challenging because of limited dedicated datasets, subtle inter-class texture differences, complex backgrounds, and scale variation. This work evaluated whether task-oriented multi-scale feature fusion and attention-based feature enhancement can improve YOLOv8s for bark-texture-based tree species detection. To this end, the Tree_bark dataset was constructed, containing 134 annotated classes and 8216 valid images, and YOLOv8s was used as the baseline detector. Three multi-scale enhancement strategies, three lightweight attention mechanisms, and their fused configuration were systematically compared under the same data split and evaluation setting. On the validation set, the baseline YOLOv8s achieved a mAP@0.5 of 0.443, a mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.339, and a Recall of 0.400. The final fused D1 model, combining WeightedConcat_B1 and EMA, showed the highest overall performance among the compared settings under the current experimental setting, with a mAP@0.5 of 0.485, a mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.365, and a Recall of 0.435. Compared with the baseline, D1 improved mAP@0.5 by 0.042, mAP@0.5:0.95 by 0.026, and Recall by 0.035. These results indicate that moderate adaptive multi-scale fusion and lightweight attention enhancement can improve bark-texture-based tree species detection in complex natural scenes. The proposed framework provides a useful reference for fine-grained tree species detection based on bark texture, although further validation across broader regions and more complex field conditions is still needed.

title: Plant Leaf Disease Localization Using Grad-CAM
abstract: Infectious illnesses are widespread among high-value Solanaceous crops (predominantly tomatoes and potatoes) and present many difficulties to food security worldwide. Classic diagnostic techniques tend to be labor intensive, subjective, and ultimately rely on the individual experience of the person performing the test or assessment. Due to these limitations, yield losses can occur and responses can be delayed. This paper proposes a full multi-stage deep learning framework that aims to quantify the degree of severity and classify multiple pathogens accurately. Our proposed architecture uses a MobileNetV2 backbone and is reported to have achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.99 when applied to 15 different states of health. We also validated the results by generating severity estimates (for example, a severity estimate of "35.42 percent was calculated"). In addition, we used gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) to provide a visual representation of the morphological signals that were used in the determination of the diagnostic results so as to assist with the interpretation of the results and to mitigate the "black box" nature of the deep neural network.

title: OkraSqueezeNet: A Lightweight CNN with Bayesian Optimization for Real-Time Ladies Finger Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Ladies finger (Abelmoschus esculentus), also name as okra or bhindi, is one important vegetable crop what grow mostly in tropical and subtropical place like India. Farmers is facing big loss many times because of leaf disease cause by fungal, bacterial, and viral thing. This disease not easy to see in starting time, and old way of checking by hand is slow, not correct, and need expert person which many small farmers not have. This work makes OkraSqueezeNet, a light weight brain like network (CNN) for find six common diseases in ladies finger leaf, train with Bayesian setting and can work on phone picture without any man help. A new set of picture name Ladies Finger Leaf Disease (LFLD), having 1,700 farm taken photo in seven group (Good, Alternaria Leaf Spot, Cercospora Leaf Spot, Downy Mildew, Leaf Curly Virus, Phyllosticta Leaf Spot, and Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus), was get from real farm in India. Trick with picture like turn, flip, blur, cut, and light change was use on teach data. The model gets 97.14% right answer with good score in all measure, do better than EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV3, ResNet, InceptionV3, and VGG16. With size only 4.82 MB, it good for put in mobile. An app make with Flutter was also build for farmer to check disease right in field in real time.

title: A Critical Comparative Survey of ML/DL Approaches for Late Blight Detection and Prediction for Guinean Agriculture
abstract: Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) remains one of the most devastating diseases for staple crops. This survey benchmarks CNN (AlexNet, VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet) and RNN architectures (LSTM, GRU) and hybrid multimodal frameworks. Our analysis reveals that ResNet-50 offers the best accuracy-to-parameter trade-off for image detection (90-99 %), while LSTM outperforms GRU for long-term temporal dependencies in disease risk prediction. We identify four structural limitations: over-reliance on the PlantVillage benchmark, near-total absence of West African training data (the rare African studies (Tanzania, Cameroon) confirm a $\mathbf{3 2 \%} \mathbf{F 1}$-score drop in real-world conditions), neglect of deployment constraints for resource-limited environments, and insufficient integration of image and climate modalities. Based on this analysis, we propose a hybrid CNN-LSTM reference architecture and formulate concrete recommendations for its adaptation to the Guinean agricultural context.

title: Deep Learning–based Detection of Mango Leaf Diseases and Nutrient Deficiencies using DenseNet-121
abstract: Mango (Mangifera indica L) is considered to be one of the most useful fruits in the world and plays a major role in terms of nutrition and revenues more so among farmers in tropical and subtropical areas. Nonetheless, major issues caused by pests and deficiency of nutrients are posing threats to the production of mangoes. These have been leaf diseases, nutrient deficiencies which may cause massive losses in production. The conventional methods of inspecting these issues rely mostly on the eye of the farmer, are time consuming and are not easy to be used by the small farmers. The paper will consider this critical concern but the automated tool will be presented that applies deep learning to study mango leaf health. The suggested system is based on DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network and transfer learning. It is capable of categorizing the mango leaf condition into eight groups; seven diseases and one healthy group. These diseases are Bacterial Canker, Powdery Mildew, anthracnose, Gall Midge, Sooty Mould, Die Back and Cutting weevil. Since certain diseases are similar to the lack of specific nutrients, it is also possible to detect potential problems with nutrients with the help of the system. The model was trained using an equal number of high-resolution leaf images of 4,000 balancing high and low and achieved a 98.75 percent accuracy on validation. Its computational requirements are ideal in the use on a mobile device. This research will make precision agriculture successful as it will offer rapid, precise, and viable diagnostic tests, thereby linking innovated artificial intelligence and the actual existence of farming.

title: Multi-Modal Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Robust In-Field Plant/Crop Disease Detection with Explainability (XAI)
abstract: Timely and precise identification of Plant/Crop diseases continues to be a significant problem in the agricultural sector, especially in developing countries. While there have been improvements in Deep Learning including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the performance of many DL models still deteriorate in the-field/on-site due to the limited diversity of datasets, the lack of Explainability (Proper XAI Framework) and computational resource restrictions. In this paper, we present a multi-modal Deep Learning Framework for in-field Plant/Crop Disease Detection that is lightweight. Using a customized MobileNetV3 model with integrated environmental metadata (e.g. temperature, humidity, Soil Condition). To solve the problem of fine-grained subtype classification for Plant/Crop Disease images with scarce resources, this paper proposes a multi-stage information fusion based lightweight model enhanced by an attention mechanism model. Built on MobileNetV3, this paper introduces a multi-stage fusion method to extract the "theme" contained-rich image information in Plant/Crop Disease images. Furthermore, during the first stage of feature extraction, we present the Selective Kernel (SK) Attention Mechanism, and in the last two steps, we embed the Squeeze-Excitation Coordinate Attention (SCA) Mechanism to obtain deeper semantic and low-level feature extraction. The final feature representations used for sub-type classification are selected from the map weights derived at each stage. Moreover, we integrate Grad-CAM-based visual explanations to enhance model comprehensibility and agriculturalist trust. In addition, we incorporate Grad-CAM-based visual explanations to make the model more interpretable to farmers. It enables identifying relevant regions of an input image that contribute to the CNN’s classification decision. Extensive experiments across three agro-climatic zones and multiple Plants/crops types (Wheat, Potato, Tomato, Rice, Maize etc.) demonstrate its ultra-modern performance, with over 96% average accuracy in varied field conditions and real-time inference capabilities (<200ms). Our Proposed MobileNetV3 model (Selective Kernel (SKA) + Squeeze-Excitation Coordinate Attention (SCA) Mechanism) achieves high classification accuracy while remaining deployable on Smart Phones/Edge Devices. We assessed and contrasted their performances on the basis of various performance evaluation metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score and confusion matrix. This work represents a significant step toward Practical, Accessible and Explainable AI Solution in Smart & Precision agriculture.

title: Intelligent Deep Learning Systems for Aquatic Weed Detection: Models, Adaptation Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: The unregulated growth of aquatic weeds is a serious threat to freshwater ecosystems because of the loss of biodiversity, decreased water quality, and disruption of socio-economic activities. Conventional monitoring techniques that rely on manual surveys are labor-intensive, limited in spatial coverage, and impractical for larger or more remote water bodies. Although there is promising modern work using deep learning (DL) and remote sensing for weed detection in agricultural systems, research in aquatic environments remains limited. In this review, we discuss DL models, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), U-Nets, and generative models and remote sensing approaches including Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imaging and satellite data, with a focus on their transition from use on land to in aquatic systems. The review will also discuss challenges that are unique to aquatic weed detection such as spectral noise caused by the water surface, seasonal variability, and lack of annotated datasets. A regionally specific case study on Surinsar–Mansar Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is discussed in terms of these challenges. Finally, we present a research roadmap including incentivizing the development of open aquatic weed datasets, combining multimodal sensing with DL models, and using explainable AI in decision-making for ecological management. Overall, the review aims to synthesize the use of terrestrial ecosystem weed monitoring and application of it in aquatic ecosystems.

title: Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Early Detection of Rice Leaf Diseases Using CNN-SVM and FRRSA-LeNet Models
authors: M. N. V. V. Sai Babu
abstract: This paper suggests an improved deep learning model to predict the early symptoms of rice leaf diseases with hybrid models. Two architectures were constructed and tested: a CNN SVM hybrid model, a combination of convolutional feature extraction and Support Vector Machine classification, and an FR-RSA optimized LeNet model, a combination of the Fractional Remora Reptile Search Algorithm to optimize the parameters of the model. The models were trained and evaluated using a data set of 5,932 rice leaf images of ten disease classes. CNN SVM model reached an accuracy of 86.9 percent which is high in class-specific classification especially in Bacterial Leaf Blight and Neck Blast. FR-RSA LeNet model had better overall performance with 97.5% accuracy, 0.978 precision, 0.980 recall and 0.977 F1-score. It provides a solution to diagnose agricultural disease in real time by deploying a user-friendly web application connected to a MobileNet-based irrelevance detection unit, which allows deploying the application in the field which is practical and scalable.

title: Rice Leaf Disease Classification with Ultra-lightweight Hybrid Deep Learning Model
abstract: Rice serves as an essential food source for more than 50% of people worldwide, and its productivity is often affected by foliar diseases that appear as small variations in color and texture of leaves. Accurate classification of such diseases is difficult in image processing due to high visual similarity among disease types and the presence of environmental noise. In this paper, we propose an ultra-lightweight hybrid deep learning (DL) framework, SE-EfficientNetB0, that combines EfficientNet-B0 with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention with the aim of improving the way the model captures both spatial and channel-based details. The proposed model has been trained over a combined dataset consisting of six classes of rice leaf diseases, which have been compiled from various publicly available sources. The architecture attains high classification accuracy with limited computational overhead by utilizing transfer learning coupled with SE-based feature refinement for maintaining the robustness and generalization of the model across various tasks. Our experimentation results reveal that the model classifies the disease classes very well, attaining an accuracy of 98.53%. Performance metrics consisting of F1-score, precision, confusion matrix, and recall analysis further confirm the model’s ability to distinguish between the disease classes. The empirical evaluation was conducted to compare SE-EfficientNetB0 model with other variants in the EfficientNet family. Among them, EfficientNetB0 emerged as the most efficient, noted for its smaller parameter count, lower computational cost, and reduced resource needs.

title: A Bio-inspired EfficientNet Framework for Accurate Mango Leaf Disease Classification

Deep Learning Framework (DLF) for Video Analysis for anomaly applying Techniques on Edge Devices, Leveraging Multimodal Fusion and Self-Supervised Machine Learning to Reduce Dependence on Datasets for Deduction in Chilli Crop Cultivation
abstract: A deep learning to perform anonymous video analysis involves processing video footage to extract specific data, such as behavioral patterns or anomalies, while preventing the identification of individuals. This field, known as privacy-preserving deep learning, uses specialized frameworks to apply anonymization techniques and safeguard private data. A high-fidelity deep-learning pipeline for early pre-symptomatic pest detection in Chilli crop cultivation is presented. The system interleaves topological data analysis, specifically persistent homology computed on modality-augmented embeddings, with classical statistical, spectral, and dynamical descriptors, and fuses persistence-image vectorisations with gradient-boosted and convolution classifiers. Multimodal fusion and self-supervised learning to reduce dependence on ordered labeled datasets as inputs comprise soil physicochemical indices, microclimatic time series, leaf-based hyper spectral signatures, pheromone and sticky-trap counts collected across multiple experimental plots and contiguous crop cycles. Preprocessing implements temporal alignment, Hamper outlier rejection, robust scaling, and locality-preserving matrix completion; recurrence quantification metrics and constrained nonnegative matrix factorization are used to summarize dynamical and spectral structure. Victories-Rips filtrations are constructed under Mahalanobis scaling, persistence diagrams are converted to normalized persistence images, and witness-sub sampling is employed to comprise combinatorial complexity. Evaluation under nested, leakage-averse time-series cross-validation demonstrates that persistence-augmented models yield an AUPRC improvement of approximately 0.12, increase recall at a 10% false-alarm rate by approximately 0.16, and provide median lead-time gains of about 2.4 days versus classical baselines. Ablation analyses attribute complementary predictive value to H0 and H1 channels. The results indicate that topological summaries materially enhance pre-symptomatic detection robustness and timeliness in precision-agronomy contexts. Despite these improvements, deployment considerations and scalable approximations are discussed to facilitate operational translation and validation.

title: Generative AI Framework for Image Captioning of Tomato Leaves in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Automatic generation of natural language descriptions from visual data is a challenging task. Conventional techniques for text generation focused on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory); however, transformer-based models have recently achieved significant improvements. The proposed framework provides an integrated pipeline for tomato leaf disease analysis by integrating disease classification and image captioning. The framework utilizes a fine-tuned Swin transformer to categorize leaf images into different disease classes and BLIP-2 to generate a real-time caption of the uploaded image, enabling automatic detection and description of tomato plant health conditions to support informed decision making in disease management. Additionally, GradCAM visualization highlights the diseased region in uploaded test images to enhance interpretability. The performance of the generated captions is evaluated using BLEU, METEOR, and ROUGE_L. Experimental results demonstrate that farmers can access both textual and visual insights, supporting more informed decision-making.

title: Automated Banana Nutrient Deficiency Diagnosis Using EfficientNetB3
abstract: The aim of this study is to identify the nutrientdeficiency detection in banana leaves using the EfficientNetB3 model and compare it with the DenseNet201 model to achieve more accuracy for classification. In this study, two deeplearning models were used. Group 1 used DenseNet201 to classify different nutrient deficiencies in banana leaves, while Group 2 used EfficientNetB3. The samples of 7047 images apply to improved features for better identification of leaf patterns compared to DenseNet201. The DenseNet201 model gives accuracy 92%. The proposed model EfficientNetB3 gives a higher accuracy of 94%. This shows that EfficientNetB3 gives clearer and more classifications. The performance improved in statistically significant value$(p<0.05)$. Banana nutrient deficiency for classification of the EfficiencientNetB3 model gives higher results compared to DenseNet201 model.

title: From images to insights: Using a convolutional neural network to improve powdery mildew severity detection in mungbean
abstract: To efficiently identify powdery mildew (PM) severity in mungbean leaves, we developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approach and validated its effectiveness against human evaluation. We fine-tuned an EfficientNet-B3 pre-trained model, which, in our related studies, performed better than re-implemented Inception V3 models. The CNN was trained on 90% of the images (2 880) for training and 10% (320) for validation, with data augmentation applied using Python and TensorFlow. The model obtained 82.10% and 73.03% as training and validation accuracies after 14 epochs, respectively. Further analysis with an additional 15 datasets revealed PM disease indices ranging from 2.03 (resistance) to 6.45 (high susceptibility). The concordance between AI-predicted and human-assessed PM severity was 74.4% (adjusted R2: 72.4%), with an average root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.854 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.715, indicating moderate predictive error. Comparison of our developed AI-based application prototype on smartphones with expert evaluations yielded a strong correlation (r = 0.992**, R2 = 0.984), suggesting that this tool can effectively estimate PM severity across mungbean cultivars. The application shows considerable promise, and further optimisation and strategic dissemination efforts will enhance its adoption among farmers.

title: Forage Crop Classification in Heterogeneous Environments Using UAV, Machine Learning, and RGB-Multispectral Fusion
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
authors: Alexandre Maniçoba da Rosa Ferraz Jardim
Lady Daiane Costa de Sousa Martins
abstract: The integration of RGB and multispectral imagery captured by Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) combined with machine learning techniques presents a promising approach for the classification of forage crops in heterogeneous agricultural systems. This study evaluated the predictive performance of 19 machine learning algorithms using RGB, multispectral (MSI), and combined RGB + MSI data. XGBoost consistently demonstrated the best balance between accuracy, generalization, and computational efficiency, achieving high performance across multiple evaluation metrics, particularly when using the fused dataset. Although Random Forest (RF) showed competitive accuracy, it was outperformed in terms of generalization and processing time. Hyperparameter tuning and model blending failed to improve predictive performance and, in some cases, led to performance declines, especially in the classification of phenotypically similar classes. The analysis revealed that model errors were concentrated among crops with similar spectral and structural characteristics, such as Mombac¸a grass, Tanzania grass, and forage cactus clones, underscoring challenges in distinguishing between such groups even at high spatial resolutions. These findings emphasize the importance of data quality, feature selection, and model interpretability in remote sensing-based classification tasks. The results have practical implications for precision agriculture, supporting more accurate crop monitoring through UAV-based remote sensing. Future research should incorporate variable selection methods, agronomic data, and deep learning approaches to enhance classification in complex agricultural environments.

title: Autonomous Edge AI Solution for Post-Harvest Mango Tommy Classification
abstract: Colombian mango export industry faces significant challenges in post-harvest classification processes, relying predominantly on manual inspection methods that limit competitiveness in international markets. Rural agricultural zones lack reliable internet connectivity and computational infrastructure, preventing the adoption of cloud-based Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions. This paper presents an autonomous edge computing approach for Tommy mango classification that operates entirely on embedded devices without external connectivity requirements. We developed and implemented a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture on the MaixCam platform, achieving 96.33% accuracy in real-world tests while processing images in 70.3ms. The system outperformed human expert classification (87.00%) by 9.33 percentage points and demonstrated 30-fold improvement in processing speed. Our solution addresses critical infrastructure limitations in developing agricultural regions while maintaining export quality standards compliance. The autonomous operation, low power consumption (1.5W), and portable design make this approach viable for widespread adoption in resource-constrained environments.

title: A Plot-to-Track Association Framework Based on Graph Representation Learning for Compact HFSWR
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: To address plot-to-track association ambiguities caused by low spatial resolution and measurement uncertainties of compact high-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) operating in complex maritime environments, a hybrid framework integrating a target state prediction method based on Transformer model and a plot-to-track association method using graph-based feature representation is proposed. In the target state prediction stage, the Transformer model employs self-attention mechanisms to capture long-term temporal dependencies in historical track data to improve the prediction accuracy of the plot-to-track association gate center. In the plot-to-track association stage, a graph autoencoder (GAE) is used to extract graph structure features of candidate measured plots from their corresponding range-Doppler (R-D) spectra. The GAE encodes the diffusion patterns and spatial correlations of radar echoes on the R-D spectrum into discriminative graph feature vectors. The graph feature vectors, which can enhance both inter-target discrimination and target-clutter differentiation, serve as the basis for association similarity computation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces target state prediction errors and suppresses false plot-to-track associations, achieving an average tracking time on target of 135.6 minutes, which is improved by 36% compared with the baseline method (motion model-based target state prediction combined with nearest neighbor data association using kinematic parameters).

title: Explainable and Robust Deep Learning for Banana Leaf Disease Classification: A Comparative Study of MobileNet, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0 With Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and Statistical Validation
abstract: Banana cultivation is significantly affected by fungal and foliar diseases, leading to substantial yield losses worldwide. Early and accurate detection is therefore essential for sustainable crop management. This study presents a comparative evaluation of three convolutional neural network architectures - MobileNet, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0 - for automated classification of banana leaf diseases using the BananaLSD dataset. The dataset includes four classes: Cordana leaf spot, Pestalotiopsis leaf spot, Black Sigatoka, and healthy leaves. To enhance robustness, Focal Loss and a Convolutional Block Attention Module are integrated into an improved MobileNet variant. Model interpretability is achieved using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), while robustness is evaluated through stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Statistical significance is assessed using McNemar’s test and Cochran’s Q test. Results show that ResNet50 achieves the highest test accuracy (99.24%) and macro-area under the curve (0.9997), while MobileNet achieves comparable performance (99.08% accuracy; macro-area under the curve = 0.9993) with significantly lower computational cost. Cross-validation confirms the stability of MobileNet (0.9915 ± 0.0066). Statistical analysis reveals significant overall differences among models (Q = 29.65, p < 0.001) but no significant difference between MobileNet and ResNet50 (p = 0.625). Grad-CAM visualizations confirm biologically meaningful lesion localization. These findings highlight MobileNet as an efficient and reliable solution for real-time banana disease detection.

title: Strategies in quantitative trait locus mapping for complex traits in maize
abstract: Maize ( Zea mays L.) is central to global food security and agricultural sustainability, serving as an important source of food, animal feed, and renewable bioenergy. However, improving maize productivity remains challenging because many key agronomic traits are complex, polygenic characteristics shaped by genetic networks and environmental interactions. Quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping has become an essential tool for dissecting these genetic architectures, and thousands of QTLs associated with important maize traits have been identified. This review provides a comprehensive examination of modern QTL mapping methodologies, including innovative population designs, high-throughput phenotyping systems, advanced genotyping technologies, and robust statistical approaches. We also discuss how emerging technologies, such as AI/machine learning (ML) and multi-omics integration, are transforming QTL analysis by improving the precision of gene discovery and trait prediction. These advances are reshaping maize breeding strategies and providing new opportunities to develop high-yielding, climate-resilient maize varieties that can help address the challenges of population growth and climate change.

title: Phenological Windows for UAV and PlanetScope Monitoring of Greenhouse Gas Fluxes in AWD Rice on the Peruvian North Coast
abstract: Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation reduces CH4 emissions from flooded rice but amplifies N2O pulses; identifying candidate phenological windows for the remote screening of greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes remains challenging with small datasets. In a single-site, single-season exploratory study at INIA Vista Florida (Lambayeque, Peru), eight UAV flights were paired with eight PlanetScope SuperDove scenes (|Δ|≤1 d) and closed-chamber CH4, N2O and CO2 fluxes under four water regimes (CF, AWD5, AWD10, AWD20; 96 sub-plot × date observations). Multivariate explanatory power was assessed by bootstrap Ridge regression on each sensor’s native predictors (VI + GLCM + Tmean for the UAV, VI for PlanetScope). Maximum tillering (79 DAS) emerged as a candidate UAV window, ranking in the top three for all gases through GLCM textures, whereas PlanetScope peaked at Mid-boot and Late-boot (103–107 DAS), with median R2˜UAV at 0.34–0.71 and R2˜Planet at 0.20–0.60. Nested Leave-One-Plot-Out (LOPO) validation gave RCV2 between +0.57 and +0.69 for four of six platform × gas combinations (UAV-CH4 and Planet-N2O stayed weak), and Tmean was decisive for N2O on the UAV (ΔR2=+0.48). Repeating the stage selection inside every LOPO fold preserved the leading combinations and their ranking. These exploratory windows and sensor-native descriptors need multi-site, multi-season validation before operational use.

title: High-Accuracy Remote Sensing Identification of Winter Wheat Based on Feature Selection and Cross-Temporal Fusion in Shandong Province, China
abstract: Accurate crop distribution mapping using multi-temporal remote sensing has become increasingly important for agricultural monitoring and management. However, existing methods often rely on the direct stacking of multi-temporal features, which leads to feature redundancy and reduced model efficiency. To address this issue, this study proposes a winter wheat identification framework that integrates growth-stage ranking, key spectral variable selection, and cross-temporal feature fusion. Taking Shandong Province as the study area, eight typical growth stages during the 2023–2024 winter wheat growing season were analyzed using Sentinel-2 imagery. Random Forest models were first constructed for each growth stage to evaluate discriminative ability. Then, spectral variable contributions were quantified using permutation importance, and key spectral variables were selected under correlation constraints. The progressive accumulation model (PAM) was then developed according to the ranking of discriminative ability across different growth stages, while the cross-temporal fusion model (CTFM) was constructed by extracting inter-stage mean values (mean) and inter-stage differences (diff) of key variables. The results show that the feature space was reduced from 64 dimensions (8 stages × 8 variables) to 16 key variables, substantially improving feature representation efficiency. Among the eight growth stages, the jointing, overwintering, heading, and grain-filling stages exhibited relatively strong discriminative ability. In the cross-temporal experiments, CTFM M6, which integrates information from the top six growth stages ranked by discriminative ability, achieved an overall accuracy (OA) of 0.9658 and a user’s accuracy (UA) of 0.9609 using only 10 fused features, providing the best balance between identification accuracy and feature dimensionality. Based on this model, a 10 m resolution winter wheat distribution map of Shandong Province was generated, and the estimated planting area showed high consistency with statistical yearbook data. These results demonstrate that the proposed strategy can effectively reduce feature dimensionality while maintaining high identification accuracy, providing an efficient and scalable approach for regional-scale remote sensing mapping of winter wheat.

title: A novel approach for crop disease detection using transfer-learning-based deep convolutional neural networks
abstract: Abstract Crop production quality can be enhanced through effective early stage monitoring of crops. In contemporary agriculture, precision farming systems that incorporate advanced technologies, such as drones, are employed for monitoring. Nevertheless, current models lack the ability to be applied broadly across various agricultural settings, leading to the suboptimal detection of crop diseases. Therefore, this study proposes a novel method for monitoring crop diseases using the Transfer-Learning-based Deep Convolutional Neural Network technique. The process commenced with the collection of a multi-crop multi-disease dataset, followed by data preprocessing through the application of Bilateral Filtering and Partial Dynamic Range Adjustment with Histogram Equalization. Subsequently, the dimensionality of the images was reduced using the Multi-Weighted Covariance Matrix Component Analysis method, and the data were organized using the K-Means Clustering algorithm. In addition, various features were extracted, with the most relevant features selected using the Mountain Gazelle Pareto Front Optimizer algorithm. To identify distinct disease characteristics, a Multidimensional Feature Distribution plot was created using the chosen features. Ultimately, the assessed spectral index of the clustered color bands, optimal features, and Multidimensional Feature Distribution plot were used to detect multi-crop diseases using the proposed Transfer Learning based Dynamic Contextual Feature Pooled Convolutional Neural Network model. The effectiveness of the proposed method was evaluated through an experimental analysis using a publicly accessible dataset. The proposed method demonstrated accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score values of 98.09%, 97.24%, 97.58%, and 97.99%, respectively, which is higher than those of existing methods.

title: Artificial intelligence for climate change mitigation and adaptation: A domain-structured review of methods, applications, and research gaps for seven high-impact domains
LSL-YOLO11n: a YOLO11n-based model for maize leaf disease detection in complex field environments
abstract: Maize leaf diseases in field environments often exhibit large variations in lesion scale, irregular morphology, blurred boundaries, and complex backgrounds. These factors pose challenges for existing detection models, particularly in detecting small lesions and achieving precise bounding-box localization. To address these issues, this study proposes LSL-YOLO11n, a maize leaf disease detection model based on the YOLO11n framework. The proposed model improves feature representation, localization quality modeling, and bounding-box regression to enhance disease detection performance under complex field conditions. Experiments were conducted on a dataset containing 15,119 images and 29,366 annotated instances across eight categories, including seven maize disease categories and healthy leaves. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model, ablation experiments, comparative experiments with mainstream object detection models, and visual detection analyses were carried out. The ablation results show that the improved components contribute positively to the overall detection performance. LSL-YOLO11n achieves a Precision of 84.4%, Recall of 73.9%, and mean Average Precision (mAP) of 83.3%, which is 3.1 percentage points higher than that of the baseline YOLO11n model. Compared with YOLOv8n, YOLOv9t, YOLOv10n, and YOLOv12n, the proposed model improves mAP by 4.7, 3.3, 5.3, and 10.9 percentage points, respectively. The visual detection results further indicate that LSL-YOLO11n performs more stably in complex backgrounds and small-lesion scenarios. These findings provide technical support for rapid maize disease recognition and intelligent field monitoring.

title: Automated hyperspectral data collection system for monitoring greenhouse plant health
abstract: Purpose Hyperspectral sensing (HS) offers strong potential for plant health monitoring, but its application in greenhouse environments is limited by dynamic conditions and the lack of automated canopy-scale data collection. This study aimed to develop an automated HS sensing platform and preprocessing workflow to improve data quality under greenhouse conditions. Methods A mobile canopy-scale HS sensing system was developed by integrating boom-based positioning, depth-guided sensing distance control, sunlight monitoring, and automated calibration. The system was evaluated in a production-style greenhouse through five independent tomato bacterial spot experiments. Environmental effects on spectral measurements were examined, and spectra affected by transient lighting changes were removed. Preprocessing effectiveness was evaluated using sample-to-centroid distance analysis, spectral variability analysis, threshold-based classification metrics, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) from logistic regression and linear SVM models. Results Seasonal greenhouse variability produced measurable spectral differences across experiments, while no meaningful AM and PM differences were observed between the two daily measurement times. Increased air moisture introduced higher near-infrared spectral noise, and short-term transportation affected early spectral responses. After preprocessing, healthy and inoculated groups showed reduced spectral variability. Despite the smaller quality-screened dataset, preprocessing improved all reported threshold-based classification metrics for both classifiers. ROC-AUC also increased, indicating improved threshold-independent discrimination between healthy and inoculated samples. Conclusion The automated HS sensing system improved greenhouse-collected spectral data quality and provided higher-quality data for downstream analysis. Although the linear baseline classifiers were not suitable for practical commercial disease diagnosis, systematic preprocessing improved the usability of canopy-scale HS data collected under dynamic greenhouse conditions.

title: CropVisionAI: A CNN-Based Approach Using MobileNetV2 for Plant Disease Detection and Classification via Streamlit
abstract: Agriculture is part of the backbone of food security of the world but crop diseases are still a threat to crop productivity and livelihood of farmers all over the world. Early and accurate detection of infected crops is very instrumental in the reduction of yield loss and provision of sustainable agricultural activities. The suggested CropVision AI framework tailored MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network, which has the ability of automating the plant diseases recognition, classification and quantitative prediction of the severity by relying on the deep learning model. The PlantVillage benchmark dataset (20,638 labeled samples and 15 disease and healthy leaf classifications of tomato, potato, and bell pepper plants) was used to be trained. The data preprocessing and data augmentation methods helped to increase model generalization, and transfer learning contributed to the better classification results. The proposed system was over 95 per cent accurate and was implemented as a real-time diagnosis system based on uploaded leaf images using a Streamlit interface. Besides sending the type of the disease, the model determines the level of severity of the disease to help in effective and timely management of crops. The comparative analysis of MobileNetV2 versus VGG16, ResNet50, and InceptionV3 showed that the latter is an optimal model between the ability of accuracy and the capacity to compute goals in smart agriculture.

title: Combining the time-series of vegetation index during the optimal window with dynamic canopy physiological features for soybean grain protein prediction
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: A CNN and Transformer-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Plant Species Classification in Real-World Environments
abstract: Plant recognition plays a vital role in agriculture and biodiversity monitoring, and deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), has gained increased attention for automating this task. However, CNNs have a limitation in their ability to handle complex patterns due to the difficulty in capturing global contextual information. Furthermore, plant datasets are often created in laboratory environments that minimize discrimination challenges, enabling the analysis of model performance. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model, HDL-PlantNet, for real-world plant recognition on the primary dataset, the Cyprus Seasonal Flora Image Dataset (CSFID), comprising 27 plant species. The HDL-PlantNet model integrates an EfficientNetV2-S convolutional backbone with a Transformer encoder to capture both spatial contextual and long-range dependencies. Additionally, the Swedish Leaf Dataset is used as a supplementary dataset to analyze the consistency of the HDL-PlantNet under controlled environments. Five benchmark CNN models are used for comparative evaluation, and statistical tests and an ablation study are conducted to assess the results. The proposed model achieved the highest observed Macro-F1 and Macro-AUC scores among the evaluated models, reaching 90.06% and 99.59%, respectively. The results demonstrate that combining convolutional and Transformer architectures yields computationally effective performance in fine-grained plant classification while maintaining a compact model size suitable for further research. This study contributes to real-time plant identification studies and supports informed ecological decision-making.

title: Characteristic wavelength selection for rice blast based on hyperspectral remote sensing and deep convolutional neural networks
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperspectral remote sensing technology is one of the key technical methods for detecting rice blast in the field, but existing hyperspectral dimensionality reduction methods still suffer from information redundancy and insufficient feature interpretability. This study aimed to develop a feature wavelength selection method integrating deep learning and model attribution analysis to extract key spectral features across different disease severity levels. RESULTS: A residual network model Dilated Convolution and Deformable Convolution-Residual Network (DCR-ResNet) combining dilated convolution and deformable convolution was constructed to deeply mine spectral features across varying disease severities. Meanwhile, the Integrated Gradient (IG) and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) methods were combined to enable the selection of spectral wavelengths. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated using statistical analysis (transformed divergence, within-class scatter) and modeling analysis. Findings reveal that the spectral feature wavelengths identified by DCR-ResNet in conjunction with the IG-GradCAM approach exhibit excellent inter-class separability and intra-class compactness. Furthermore, when benchmarked against conventional dimensionality reduction techniques such as Successive Projections Algorithm, Random Frog, and Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling, the Support Vector Machine, Extreme Learning Machine, and Random Forest models developed using IG-GradCAM-selected feature wavelengths demonstrate superior classification performance. The overall accuracy reaches 85.9%, 85.5% and 86.2%, with kappa values of 81.3%, 80.6% and 81.6%, respectively. CONCLUSION: The feature wavelength selection method combining DCR-ResNet with IG-GradCAM not only improves the accuracy of hyperspectral feature extraction but also provides an efficient and feasible approach for the precise identification of rice blast. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: A Lightweight Deep Learning Architecture for Multi-Crop Disease Detection Using Custom CNN and EfficientNet-B0
abstract: Improving agricultural production and maintaining global food security depend on the early and precise diagnosis of crop diseases. Manual diagnosis is often laborintensive, subjective, and unsuitable for large-scale farming. To address these limitations, this study proposes a custom lightweight CNN integrated with EfficientNet-B0 and depthwise separable convolution layers for automated detection and classification of diseases in five major crops: corn, potato, rice, wheat, and sugarcane. A dataset of 15,211 leaf images covering 17 healthy and diseased classes was constructed from real-time field data, with data augmentation applied to address class imbalance. The proposed model was compared with three pretrained CNN architectures: VGG16, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model attained a test accuracy of 99.12%, outperforming VGG16 (97.32%), MobileNetV2 (96.02%), and EfficientNet-B0 (95.21%). With only 4.8 million parameters, the architecture is highly efficient in computation and appropriate for real-time execution in resource-constrained agricultural situations, highlighting the potential of customized lightweight models for scalable crop disease monitoring.

title: Crop Disease Detection in Bangladesh Using ConvNeXt-Tiny and Conventional CNN with Grad-CAM Interpretability
abstract: Bangladesh plays a key role in the agricultural part of the country's economic growth. The contribution of the agricultural sectors to both GDP and the global workforce. Rice, wheat, jute, and vegetables are the primary agricultural products in Bangladesh. Farmers need an automated procedure that can grow alongside them because visual inspection is inefficient, insufficient, and not very beneficial. Deep learning enables the automatic extraction of features in image analysis. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been utilized for various agricultural tasks, such as crop disease detection, yield forecasting, and crop monitoring. This research uses a data set on crop diseases in Bangladesh and evaluates various CNN architectures, including VGG16, ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, InceptionV3, and ConvNeXt-Tiny, through several performance evaluations and Grad-CAM for interpretability. The accuracy of the 97.42%, indicate that ConvNeXt-Tiny outperforms the baseline models and that preprocessing images using methods such as bilateral filtering and CLAHE provides improved image quality. This work creates valuable knowledge for scalable AI-driven interventions to improve Bangladesh's agriculture and food security by linking the results of this work to mobile and Internet of Things (IoTs) applications.

title: Physiological and molecular mechanisms underlying crop responses to pest attack and their implications for sustainable management
A CNN-Based Intelligent Framework for Early Plant Stress Detection and Automated Remediation Recommendations in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Detecting plant stress at the very beginning is of great importance for the sustainability of agricultural production and the optimal use of resources. A new intelligent framework based on CNN is proposed in this paper that not only identifies early plant stress with a very high accuracy but also gives automated, context-sensitive remediation suggestions. Our system uses a specially designed Convolutional Neural Network architecture that is trained on a multimodal dataset consisting of the visible spectrum and other sources. The detection module achieves a stable performance of 83.5 to 84.98% accuracy over several stress categories, which is significantly better than the existing methods in the literature that usually have an accuracy range of 70 to 82%. The next step after detection with 83.5 to 84.98% accuracy is that our integrated recommendation engine quickly generates targeted prescriptive interventions, which are solely based on the type of stress diagnosed. The system provides specific guidance on fertilizer formulations, irrigation adjustments, or pesticide applications through structured knowledge-based mapping for each correctly identified condition from the test dataset. This entire process from detection to prescription demonstrates the possibility of practical deployment at the edge, thereby giving farmers actionable insights directly from visual analysis. Validation through experiments proves the system’s ability to connect automated diagnosis with immediate agricultural recommendations, thus helping precision resource management through timely, data driven interventions.

title: An Integrated Vision- and Environment-Aware Decision-Support System for Smart Harvesting
abstract: Decisions related to harvest timing and crop condition are still largely based on visual inspection and experience in many small- and medium-scale agricultural settings. Such practices make it difficult to respond consistently to changes in fruit maturity or environmental stress. Although digital tools have been proposed to support these tasks, most existing solutions focus on a single aspect, such as ripeness detection, environmental monitoring, or yield estimationwithout providing a unified basis for on-field decision making. This paper describes a locally deployable decision-support system that integrates visual assessment of fruit ripeness with environmental context and simple economic reasoning. Fruit images are analyzed to determine ripeness categories and associated confidence levels, which are then used to derive a relative yield potential indicator. In parallel, temperature and humidity measurements are interpreted through rule-based agronomic conditions to identify possible stress or diseasefavorable environments. The system favors transparent logic over black-box prediction, allowing users to understand how conclusions are formed. Operation is confined to a local area network using embedded sensing and vision at the edge, ensuring low latency and independence from continuous cloud access. By supporting more informed harvest decisions and reducing avoidable losses, the proposed system contributes toward Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger) and Sustainable Development Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). The work demonstrates the value of practical integration across vision, sensing, and decision logic in real agricultural contexts.

title: A Large-Scale Multi-Crop Leaf Disease Dataset and Benchmarking of Deep Learning Models with Explainable Predictions
abstract: Early and timely diagnosis of plant diseases is very important for sustained crop production and sustainable food security. Traditional manual inspection methods are expensive in terms of labor, prone to error and impractical for large scale agricultural monitoring. Although deep learning applications in automated disease detection have been promising, existing datasets are mostly small, fragmented, crop-specific, or obtained under controlled environments and unable to generalize well. To overcome these limitations, in this study, a large-scale unified leaf disease dataset consisting of 143186 RGB images belonging to 86 diseased and healthy classes across 19 crop species is proposed. Several state-of-the-art pretrained convolutional neural networks namely Xception, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0 were benchmarked and achieved high classification accuracies of$98.57 \%, 98.86 \%, 97.88 \%$, and 96.66 %, respectively, with smooth and stable training convergence. Interpretability analysis with LIME shows that models are biased to disease-relevant regions of the leaves and hence make transparent and reliable predictions. This dataset and tested models provide a standard benchmark for leaf disease detection in multi-crops that will support good AI nature-based detection for practical and explainable AI solutions in agriculture.

title: Dual-Model Crop Disease Detection Using YOLOv8 and Faster R-CNN for Bangladeshi Agricultural Systems
abstract: Early and timely detection of leaf diseases is a key factor for the enhancement of crop productivity and sustainable agriculture. The existing methods do not have a consistent evaluation framework that could estimate the mutual benefits of one-stage and two-stage detection methods in multiple crop types for Bangladesh. To fill these gaps, we propose a novel plant disease detection framework that simultaneously assesses YOLOv8 and R-CNN (Region-based Convolutional Networks) models across a curated crop-specific subset of the PlantVillage dataset with five economically important Bangladeshi crops. In this work, YOLOv8 achieved an average precision of 0.99, mAP 0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.73, while Faster R-CNN obtained an average precision of 0.978, mAP 0.5:0.95 of 0.549, with precision and recall of 0.978 and 0.916. Evaluation was supported by classical detection metrics, cross-architecture comparison, and analysis of lesion features that contribute to the performance gap between one-stage and two-stage detectors. The aim of this study is to propose an effective and practical disease recognition framework by balancing accuracy with computation time using these two complementary detection strategies in order to ensure reliable and scalable monitoring of crop diseases.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and optimization of dominant and recessive morphology of cultivated land use in the Ili River Valley
abstract: In recent years, the rapid expansion and functional degradation of cultivated land have intensified the pressure on this crucial resource, and the protection of cultivated land needs urgent attention. Based on an integrated view of dominant and recessive, combined with landscape index selection, spatial mapping method, kernel density estimation, and coupling coordination degree, this study examines the spatiotemporal changes in cultivated land in the Ili River Valley from 2005 to 2020 and proposes optimization strategies. Key findings include: (1) The dominant morphology of cultivated land use shows a slow growth trend, and the recessive morphology (total function) exhibits a faster growth rate than that of the dominant morphology. (2) The coupling coordination has gradually shifted from barely coordinated and primary coordination to intermediate coordination. (3) The region is divided into three primary zones and six secondary zones, and this study proposes targeted differentiated development strategies. It is helpful to the sustainable utilization of cultivated land and the rational planning of land space in arid oasis regions.

title: Comparative Analysis of Hand-Crafted and Deep Learning Methods for Grape Leaf Disease Classification
venue: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences
abstract: This study investigates grape leaf disease classification using both hand-crafted feature extraction methods and deep learning models. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) are employed as hand-crafted approaches, while Convolutional Neural Networks, including VGG16, ResNet-50, AlexNet, GoogLeNet, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0, are utilized as deep learning methods. Experiments are conducted on two publicly available datasets, Grape400 and PlantVillage. The results demonstrate that deep learning models consistently outperform hand-crafted methods across both datasets. VGG16 achieves the highest accuracy of 98.75% on Grape400 and 99.51% on PlantVillage, while MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet-B0 also show competitive performance with accuracies exceeding 97%. In contrast, PCA and LBP yield notably lower accuracies, particularly on the Grape400 dataset. These findings confirm the effectiveness of transfer learning-based deep learning architectures for robust and accurate grape leaf disease classification, highlighting their potential application in precision agriculture.

title: Advances in spectroscopic and machine learning approaches for estimating soil organic carbon and nitrogen: a comprehensive review
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) and nitrogen (N) are fundamental indicators of soil fertility, productivity, and environmental sustainability. Traditional wet chemistry techniques, although precise in their determination, are resource-demanding, time-consuming, and, in most cases, not economical for large-scale monitoring. The growing need to adopt fast, economical, and dependable methods has seen soil spectroscopy come into the limelight as an alternative revolution. The paper is a review of up-to-date developments in soil spectroscopy to estimate SOC and N, including visible-near infrared (VNIR) and mid-infrared (MIR) spectroscopy. The use of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imaging, satellite remote sensing, and the combination with machine learning model is critically discussed. It has been reported that MIR spectroscopy offers more accurate and superior spectral characteristics of SOC and N than VNIR and that several studies have found higher prediction accuracies (R2 often in the range of 0.94–0.98 with MIR compared to 0.49–0.83 with VNIR in relation to SOC, with slightly lower but comparable trends for nitrogen) and substantially lower RMSE values because of an enhanced fundamental molecular absorption features. When used in conjunction with chemometric and machine learning models, remote sensing platforms can be used to improve the scalability of SOC and N mapping. Nevertheless, there are some issues of transferability of calibration, soil heterogeneity, and barriers to adoption in developing nations like India, where the spectrum libraries of soils and the infrastructure are not well established. The review highlights the importance of preprocessing techniques, calibration policies, and advanced algorithms, including random forests, support machines, and deep learning, to enhance the accuracy of prediction. Future studies should focus on creating massive spectral libraries, incorporating multimodal streams of data, and deploying accessible digital platforms to facilitate precision agriculture. On the whole, soil spectroscopy can transform the concept of nutrient monitoring by transforming scientific innovation into field-level implementation.

title: Multisource Data Integration for Enhanced Wheat Yield Prediction Using Optimized Ensemble Machine Learning Approaches
PestSignal: Crop Insect Detection and Prevention for Agriculture
abstract: Agricultural pest infestation reduces crop production, particularly in developing countries that still rely on manual inspection for pest monitoring. This paper presents PestSignal, an offline capable crop pest detection and prevention system built on deep learning. The system uses YOLOv11 to identify nine pest species common in Bangladeshi agricultural fields. A locally collected dataset was annotated and augmented to reflect real field conditions. The trained model was compressed through pruning and quantization for deployment on mobile and desktop devices without internet access. PestSignal also provides prevention and treatment recommendations to help farmers reduce unnecessary pesticide use. Experimental results show high detection accuracy with low inference time across the nine target classes.

title: HibiLite-CNN: Accurate Hibiscus Leaf Disease Classification with Minimal Computational Overhead
abstract: Classification of plant leaf diseases through automated computers is critical in enhancing the yield of agricultural products, and most algorithms based on deep learning use computationally intensive architectures at the expense of laboratory-collected datasets, restricting their realworld use. This paper presents a proposal of HibiLite-CNN; a task-specific lightweight convolutional neural network to perform multi-class classification of hibiscus leaf diseases based on a single dataset that was captured in a natural environment. The dataset has 1,101 images in eight disease types and the processing is done with a class-balanced augmentation with avoiding data leakage. HibiLite-CNN combines depthwise separable convolutions, residual connections, and channel-wise attention to attain a successful trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Experimental findings indicate that the proposed model can achieve a macroaveraged accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score of 0.976 using 0.23 M parameters, making it more computationallyefficient than a number of transfer learning baselines. Stable convergence and high generalization are ensured by three-fold cross-validation.
